title: MT82 Transmission Fluid Drain and Refill
introduction:
This procedure covers the MT82 manual transmission. I identify the gearbox before choosing fluid: a bottle's reassuring transmission-shaped label is no substitute for the right specification.

The drawings distinguish the low drain plug from the side fill opening marked FILL. Keep the vehicle level, drain the old fluid, close the drain opening, refill through the side opening and tighten the fill plug. Use the linked specification's transmission-fluid and capacity entries; the other materials on that reference page are not a shopping list for this fluid change.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep a parked gear selected. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect yourself while handling fluid and parts
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp parts. Failure to do so can cause serious personal injury. Consult the material safety information sheet before using the specified fluid or other specified materials; improper use can cause serious personal injury. Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

items.name: Locate the marked lifting points
items.detail: Use [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631). The underside drawing identifies lifting areas along both sides of the body, behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Locate the triangle stamped into the uni-body sheet metal or frame at each point. Lifting elsewhere can make the vehicle shift or fall and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: If using a service jack
items.detail: Choose a jack rated for the vehicle's weight, including cargo and modifications. Work on a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. After raising the vehicle, support it with floor stands before going underneath. A jack can lower unexpectedly; using it as the only support can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Keep the emergency jack and bumpers out of this job
items.detail: The vehicle-supplied jack is only for emergency replacement of a deflated tire; using it for this service can damage the vehicle. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper, because the bumper covers will be damaged.

items.name: If using a hoist
items.detail: Confirm that its capacity covers the vehicle, cargo and modifications, and position its lift arms at the points shown in the lifting reference. Incorrect positioning can cause unintended vehicle movement, serious personal injury or death. Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels unless every drive wheel is off the ground; contact with the ground can cause unintended movement with the same consequences.

items.name: Check lift clearance before raising
items.detail: Position hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering linkage to prevent damage. Before driving onto a drive-on lift, check for underbody interference. On a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped, and position the hoist to avoid damaging the axle or rear cover.

items.name: Use the matching lubricant and capacity entries
items.detail: Use Motorcraft Dual Clutch Transmission Fluid XT-11-QDC meeting WSS-M2C200-D2. The [MT82 Specifications](#/document/G1687313) list transmission fluid capacity as 2.7 qt (2.6 L). Motorcraft MT82 Transmission Additive XL-18 is required only after synchronizer replacement; an ordinary drain and refill does not by itself meet that condition. Brake fluid, grease, sealers and threadlocker elsewhere in the reference are not additional fill ingredients.

edits.text: NOTE: Keep the vehicle level for this procedure.
edits.why: Level means the vehicle itself, not merely the patch of floor beneath the lifting equipment. Preserve that attitude while draining and filling.

edits.text: Prepare and support the vehicle using [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631) (100-02 Jacking and Lifting, Description and Operation).
edits.why: The linked drawing identifies the lifting points by stamped triangles along the body sides. Use those locations and the applicable jack or hoist precautions above before working underneath.

edits.text: Remove the drain plug and allow the transmission fluid to drain. After draining, refit the drain plug and tighten it to 26 lb.ft (35 Nm).
edits.why: The illustration highlights the low plug beside the housing flange, rather than the surrounding case bolts. The tightening value applies when the plug goes back in; closing the drain opening completes this stage before fresh fluid is added.

edits.text: Remove the fill plug from the side of the transmission housing.
edits.why: The highlighted side plug sits beside the mounting bracket in the illustration. It opens the filling route, separate from the low drain opening used earlier.

edits.text: Fill the transmission through the opening marked FILL, using the Fluid Suction Gun listed under General Equipment. Use the specified transmission fluid and capacity in [Specifications](#/document/G1687313) (308-03A Manual Transmission - 6-Speed Manual Transmission – MT82, Specifications).
edits.why: I use the lubricant entry and capacity entry together: one identifies what belongs inside, and the other establishes the amount. The opening's label identifies where to deliver it; the drawing does not establish an additional fill-to-overflow rule. The specification's additive condition applies only after synchronizer replacement.

edits.text: Install the fill plug and tighten it to 26 lb.ft (35 Nm).
edits.why: This closes the side filling opening after the specified fill is complete. Use the tightening value here rather than judging tightness by feel. With the engine stopped, inspect both refitted plug areas for fluid escaping and resolve any leak before driving. Account for the tools, clear everyone from underneath, and lower the vehicle using the lifting equipment instructions while retaining the parking brake and restoring wheel restraints as the tires meet the ground. Finish fully grounded with the parked gear selected, ignition OFF and key outside. This is an ordinary post-refill check, not a diagnosis of shifting concerns.

editorialRevision.scope: Only introduction qualifier cleanup, requirements and final why. Actual MT82 scope/primary actions/35Nm unchanged; exact already trusted specifications supplied inline, bounded stationary completion.
